Title: France launches 'attempted murder' probe after petrol bomb attacks on security forces
Article:
PARIS: France on Sunday launched an attempted murder probe after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during Paris protests, as footage of an officer in flames sparked outrage.
On Saturday, clashes erupted in Paris and other cities after hundreds of thousands of people staged a third weekend of protests against soaring living costs.
The Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail.
While riots were less widespread than two weeks ago, when France experienced some of its worst unrest in years, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Saturday that the level of violence perpetrated by some was "extraordinary."
Dramatic images, including AFP photos and video, showed a homemade incendiary device exploding at the feet of a security officer in protective gear, engulfing his lower body in flames.
Prosecutors that said an investigation had been opened for "attempted murder of persons vested with public authority."
"Explosive devices were thrown at around 15 gendarmes as well as police officers," the prosecutor's office said.
Gendarmes are military police officers who are part of the French armed forces.
An assessment of the injured was ongoing, prosecutors said, adding that the reported injuries included second-degree burns.
- 'Under assault' -
The gendarme struck by the Molotov cocktail said his unit was "under assault", with glass bottles, paving stones, shards of glass, and firebombs thrown at them.
"We were hit by several significant incendiary devices," he told broadcaster RTL on condition of anonymity.
"The flammable substance was so greasy that I could feel it spreading across my skin," he said. "I kept wondering when it would stop because I really felt as though I had been coated by the heat itself."
The officer, who received minor injuries, said the leg and shin protections on his riot uniform melted.
After watching the footage of the firebomb attack that injured him, he said he was surprised by "the intensity" of the incident. The video made him realise "that we may also have come close to a catastrophe."
His unit had been on leave but was recalled ahead of the protests.
The gendarmerie said that 13 members of the officer's unit were injured, according to RTL.
No suspects "have been arrested at this stage in connection with the incident", the prosecutor's office said, adding that investigators were working to identify those responsible.
The protests come in a tense political climate, with presidential elections six months away and frontrunner Marine Le Pen vowing to restore law and order if elected next year.
Le Pen, the leader of far-right National Rally party, said on X those responsible for the firebomb attack must be "punished with the utmost severity."
Both she and Bruno Retailleau, head of the right-wing Republicans, described images of the officer in flames as "unbearable."
Left-leaning Le Figaro said: "The days of the May 1968 riots are a far cry from today, when gendarmes facing the most violent protesters wore... ties."
More than 770 people were arrested across France, the interior ministry said.
A total of 159 members of law enforcement were injured during protests and Halloween celebrations, the ministry said.
The number of shops damaged on the sidelines of Saturday's protests was significantly lower than during previous weekends, with some 20 businesses affected, according to France's Chambers of Commerce and Industry (CCI).
But CCI France voiced concern about the impact of the protests on retail activity ahead of the year-end holiday season, a peak period for businesses.

Title: Mufti Menk visits Tun M, conveys condolences over Siti Hasmah's death
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prominent preacher Mufti Menk visited Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad today to convey his condolences over the death of the former prime minister's wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali.
In a post on Threads, account holder Sulaiman an-Nuuri said Mufti Menk offered his condolences and referred to Dr Hasmah as "our mother".
He said that during the meeting, Mufti Menk shared a hadith about a man who gave water to a thirsty dog.
"Because of his kindness, Allah forgave the man's sins and admitted him into paradise.
"Mufti Menk said Allah always gives us opportunities to do good in this life, not only to dogs but to all humanity.
"The kindness and repentance of a servant can lead him to paradise. Referring to the story, Mufti Menk said Dr Hasmah's contributions and kindness to Malaysia and the ummah were immense, and prayed that Allah would grant her the highest level of paradise," the post said.
Mufti Menk is in the capital to deliver a keynote lecture at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL) today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman falls from second floor of Tampoi flat after seizure
Article:
JOHOR BARU: An 18-year-old woman was injured after she was believed to have suffered a seizure and fallen from the second floor of a flat in Tampoi.
The woman was found lying on the pavement outside the building, conscious, after the incident at about 12.20pm.
Johor Baru North acting district police chief Superintendent Azrol Anuar Nor said police received a report shortly after the incident.
"Initial investigations found that the woman was believed to have suffered a seizure while looking down over the stairwell wall before losing her balance and falling from the second floor of the flat," he said in a statement.
The woman sustained injuries to the back of her head, neck, left wrist and right leg.
She is receiving further treatment at Hospital Sultanah Aminah, he said.
Azrol said police had identified four witnesses and would record their statements to assist with the investigation.
Anyone with information can call 07-5563122, police said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman's body found caught in fishing net buoy line in Sungai Kuantan
Article:
KUANTAN: The body of an unidentified woman was found caught in a fishing net buoy line in Sungai Kuantan near Jalan Besar here today.
Kuantan police chief assistant commissioner Ashari Abu Samah said police received information about the discovery from the public at 12.38pm.
He said initial checks found the body of a woman believed to be in her 30s, wearing a red shirt and white shorts with black patterns.
"Further checks revealed bloody scratch marks on the victim's forehead, but no other injuries indicating foul play were found," he said in a statement today.
Ashari said the body was sent to Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital for a post-mortem, while the case was classified as sudden death.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Family dispute behind fight involving three men in Johor
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A family dispute is believed to have sparked a fight involving three men, including a senior citizen, outside a shop in Plentong.
Seri Alam district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Sohaimi Ishak said the three men, aged between 27 and 60, had been arrested to assist investigations.
He said police had detected a two-minute-six-second video of the incident uploaded to Facebook on Saturday.
"Initial investigations found that the three suspects were related and that the fight stemmed from a family dispute, he said in a statement today.
Sohaimi said the case was being investigated under Sections 324 and 160 of the Penal Code.
"The three suspects have been remanded for three days until Nov 3 to assist investigations," he said.
A separate 2-minute-54-second video had earlier gone viral, showing a senior citizen being allegedly pushed, kicked and slapped by a man outside a car wash in Plentong.
The footage drew criticism from social media users, who expressed sympathy for the victim and questioned the man's actions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cops probe woman over incident involving two children at KL mall
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are investigating a woman accused of pushing and hitting two children at a shopping mall in the capital.
The case came to light after a 35-second video went viral on Threads and Facebook.
The video showed a heated exchange between the children's father and the woman at the scene, drawing widespread anger from social media users.
Dang Wangi district police chief Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said police had detected the video and received an official report from the children's father.
He said the incident occurred at 3pm yesterday when the 36-year-old complainant was walking with his two children, aged 2 and 7.
"Suddenly, an unknown woman pushed his son from behind, causing him to fall, and hit his daughter on the back of the head," he said in a statement.
Ahmad Azwan said police viewed the incident seriously and were conducting an investigation.
He urged witnesses to contact police at 03-2600 2222.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar announces RM1mil allocation to aid hawkers, small traders
Article:
KAJANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has allocated RM1 million to the Ministry of Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives to coordinate assistance for associations, hawkers and small traders to help boost their income.
He said the allocation took into account the hundreds of thousands of hawkers, small traders and associations operating nationwide.
"Initially, I thought of announcing RM100,000, which is already a significant amount, but then I considered that there are hundreds of thousands of hawkers, businesses, stalls and associations across the country, so let us manage this properly.
"(The government) is providing assistance so that every year we see an increase in the income of hawkers and traders," he said at the closing ceremony of the national-level Hawkers and Small Traders Day Carnival 2026.
Also present were Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
Also in attendance was Federation of Malay Hawkers and Small Traders Associations of Malaysia (GPPPKMM) president Datuk Zainal Abidin Abd Majid.
The allocation comes amid the government's efforts to help low-income earners, including hawkers and small traders, increase their income. -- BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bukit Kuda rehab centre trespass: Cops investigate after group takes several inmates
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Police are investigating a suspected trespassing incident involving a group who entered a private rehabilitation centre in Bukit Kuda, near here, and removed several inmates without the management's permission.
Klang Utara police chief assistant commissioner Ramsay Embol said police received a report from the centre's owner on Oct 28, claiming that a group of unidentified men and women had entered the premises and taken several inmates away.
"Police confirm the incident and the case is being investigated under Section 447 of the Penal Code for criminal trespass," he said in a statement today.
Ramsay advised the public against speculating on the case, saying this could affect public order and disrupt police investigations.
Those with information about the incident can contact the Klang Utara District police headquarters at 03-32919614 or the investigating officer, Sergeant Amirul Ashraf Abd Rahim, at 011-69730086.
Earlier, a 38-second video circulated on social media showing several individuals, believed to be inmates, leaving a rehabilitation centre in Klang.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Burst tyre suspected in crash that killed couple in Batu Pahat
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A burst tyre is believed to have caused a tar-laden lorry to crush an MPV, killing a husband and wife on Jalan Yong Peng-Muar.
Batu Pahat district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said the crash occurred while the MPV was travelling from Yong Peng towards Parit Sulong.
He said the lorry, travelling in the opposite direction, was believed to have lost control after one of its tyres burst before veering off course and
crushing the MPV.
The MPV driver, Mohd Hardi Mohd Husin, 46, and his wife, Tengku Syafirana Tengku Abdullah, 44, suffered serious injuries and were pronounced dead at the scene.
Hardi sustained injuries to his head and both hands, as well as burns to several parts of his body. His wife suffered serious head and internal injuries, and burns.
Two other MPV passengers, the couple's 11-year-old adopted daughter and their 8-year-old son, sustained cuts, burns to their legs and head injuries.
The children were taken to Hospital Sultanah Nora Ismail (HSNI) for treatment, he said in a statement.
Shahrulanuar said investigations were ongoing and the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving.

Title: 1,000 Titiwangsa residents receive Deepavali food baskets
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,000 residents in the Titiwangsa parliamentary constituency received food baskets ahead of Deepavali, which falls on Nov 8.
Titiwangsa member of parliament Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the initiative was part of his regular efforts to spend time with and engage with the local community.
"It is my routine to visit the constituency every weekend. During this weekend's break, I distributed Deepavali food baskets to 1,000 recipients in the Titiwangsa parliamentary constituency," he said in a Facebook post today.
Also present at the event was Titiwangsa MIC division chief Arasu Palanysamy.
Johari said that despite differences in race, religion and culture, the spirit of a multicultural society and the celebration of diversity remained central to the country.

Title: Melaka polls: BN candidate pledges more jobs, affordable housing in Serkam
Article:
JASIN: Creating more job opportunities and providing affordable housing for young people will be among Barisan Nasional candidate Datuk Azman Abdullah's priorities if he wins the Serkam seat in the Melaka election.
Azman said his focus would be on strengthening youth development through the expansion of the Halal Hub industrial area in Serkam, particularly by creating employment opportunities linked to Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).
He said the second phase of the industrial development, which was still under construction, could provide more job opportunities for local youths.
"We have recently seen the development of the second phase of the Halal Hub industrial area.
"When young people say there are limited job opportunities, this is one of the areas we want to develop, particularly through the Halal Hub and TVET.
"Although it is still under construction, our focus is to ensure that young people in Serkam will benefit from the development," he told reporters during a campaign visit to Pantai Siring here.
Apart from employment, Azman said he was also concerned about the lack of affordable housing in Serkam, which had forced many young residents to move elsewhere after getting married.
He said the shortage of suitable housing within the constituency was among the issues he hoped to address if elected.
"One of my aspirations is to ensure that young people who get married do not have to move away from Serkam.
"We see many of them leaving because housing options within the constituency are limited.
"Although there are affordable houses in Scientex, the area is quite far from the main Serkam area and is located near the boundary with Merlimau," he said.
Azman said he would explore the possibility of identifying suitable land for more affordable housing developments, particularly for those in the B40 income group.
"We want to identify more land that can be developed into affordable housing so that young families can continue living within the Serkam constituency," he said.
On his campaign strategy, Azman acknowledged the importance of reaching out to younger voters, some of whom might not be familiar with him despite his long-standing ties to the constituency.
He said he had lived in Serkam for decades and was encouraged by the response he received during his first two days of campaigning.
"Most people here already know me because I have lived in Serkam for decades.
"However, there may be some younger voters who are not familiar with me. That is why we need to find ways to approach them.
"If we want to connect with young people, we need to understand their interests and approach them in a way they can relate to," he said.
On tourism development, Azman said Pantai Siring had considerable potential as a tourist destination, particularly during weekends and school holidays when the area attracted large crowds.
He said land acquisition for a proposed road improvement project had been completed, including the payment of compensation to affected landowners.
However, funding was still needed to widen the road and improve access to the beach.
Azman said further development would require careful planning as much of the surrounding land remained privately owned.
He also hoped to improve infrastructure and development in Pekan Umbai.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: PH candidate pledges to champion key issues in Machap Jaya
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Pakatan Harapan candidate for the Machap Jaya seat Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin has pledged to continue championing key issues involving infrastructure, welfare, the safety of children and women, road safety and the environment.
The former Wanita PKR's Information chief said the positive response she received during walkabouts since the first day of campaigning after nominations had encouraged her to continue seeking residents' support.
Her experience as the Machap Jaya assemblyman from 2018 to 2021 would be an advantage in serving residents if elected in the Melaka election.
She said her previous experience and service record were still remembered by some residents, motivating her to offer better services if given another opportunity to represent the constituency.
"I am optimistic about continuing to garner support so that I can provide better services than I did previously.
"We are now entering a new political era, and the people are more discerning. They assess candidates based on their capabilities, experience, as well as the vision and plans they bring," she said when met after a walkabout at Taman Pengkalan Indah here today.
She said greater emphasis should be placed on a political approach that prioritised concrete and clear proposals for the people, rather than a political culture dominated by disputes, insults and verbal abuse.
Ginie also wants to focus on empowering women economically and creating more job opportunities and skills development programmes for young people.
She said women, including single mothers, could benefit from opportunities to obtain certification and accreditation in childcare, opening up employment opportunities either from home or at childcare centres.
"Young people should also be given greater exposure to the opportunities available, whether through government funding or skills training.
"Based on my experience serving at Invest Melaka and engaging with the industry, there are actually plenty of opportunities for young people, particularly in high-tech industries such as semiconductors and the electrical and electronics sectors," she said.
In a separate development, Ginie said she was still awaiting responses from her two opponents to her invitation to hold an open dialogue, which would allow voters to assess each candidate's proposals and plans.
"It is not a debate or a contest of arguments. We simply want to have a dialogue, and it is not a challenge but an invitation.
"So, I am still waiting for them to suggest a date because I respect them, as each of them has a very busy campaign schedule," she said.
The Machap Jaya seat is seeing a three-cornered contest in this election, with incumbent Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem facing Ginie and Bersama candidate Prasanth Kumar Brakasam.
The constituency has 16,030 registered voters. In the 2021 state election, Ngwe retained the seat for Barisan Nasional with 3,732 votes and a majority of 938.

Title: At 81, grandfather of 35 earns PhD after mastering digital technology
Article:
BACHOK: An 81-year-old grandfather of 35 has earned a PhD despite health challenges and the need to master computers and digital technology during his studies.
Dr Abdul Ghani Muhamad graduated at Universiti Malaysia Kelantan's (UMK) convocation ceremony today.
Ghani completed his PhD in Sufism and Tariqa studies in four years, on schedule.
He said his main challenge had been managing several health conditions, including high blood pressure, prostate problems and nerve-related issues.
"I also underwent two eye surgeries during my studies and faced age-related challenges, including declining memory.
"I also had to learn to use digital technology and computers, but my children and grandchildren motivated me to complete my studies," he said when met at UMK's 16th convocation ceremony at Dewan Tuanku Canselor, Bachok campus.
Ghani said he pursued a PhD to fulfil a youthful ambition of entering university and attaining the highest level of academic qualification.
Financial constraints and family commitments had forced him to put that ambition on hold. He only had the opportunity to pursue further studies after his nine children had grown up and started families, and after he had retired as a religious teacher.
The husband of Che Norma Che Ismail, 79, who lives in Bukit Marak, said he was keen to pursue another PhD in religious studies at UMK's Faculty of Language Studies and Human Development.
Ghani was among 4,035 graduates being celebrated at this year's convocation, which comprises eight sessions running from today until Thursday.
As UMK's oldest PhD graduate, he was joined at the ceremony in Bachok by more than 20 family members, including his children, in-laws and grandchildren.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Candidates advised to respect media practitioners, says Fahmi
Article:
MELAKA: Candidates contesting in the Melaka election have been advised to respect and appreciate the presence of media practitioners throughout the campaign period, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said media practitioners should lodge police reports promptly if they encountered any uncomfortable situations while carrying out their duties.
Fahmi also encouraged media practitioners to lodge complaints with the Malaysian Media Council if their content was plagiarised or used without permission.
"We do not want any party stealing information or content from a media organisation without giving credit or acknowledging the source.
"If anything of this nature occurs, I hope members of the media affected will report it to the Malaysian Media Council," he told reporters after visiting the Communications Ministry's media centre at a hotel in Ayer Keroh here today.
Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and Information Department director-general Erwin Khairul Ahmad.
The Melaka election officially began yesterday with the nomination of candidates. Early voting is scheduled for Nov 10, while polling will take place on Nov 14, following the dissolution of the state legislative assembly effective Sept 23.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said that apart from the main media centre in Ayer Keroh, 39 National Information Dissemination Centres across Melaka had also been designated as media centres to facilitate media practitioners in carrying out their duties.
He said the centres could also serve as rest areas for media practitioners between assignments before they proceed to their next locations.
"We have also set up a Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) complaints counter for media colleagues who encounter internet connectivity problems while on duty. I also encourage them to download the MCMC Nexus application.
"This way, if there are any locations in Melaka that are 'blind spots', we hope our media colleagues can help bring them to our attention through the MCMC Nexus application," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor schools to operate as usual tomorrow despite haze
Article:
SHAH ALAM: All schools in Selangor will operate as usual tomorrow, the Selangor Education Department (JPN) said.
In a statement today, the department called on all parties to continue prioritising the health and safety of students and school personnel amid the current haze situation.
"Students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks as a precautionary measure, particularly those who are sensitive to haze conditions.
"Schools, parents and guardians are also advised to remain alert to developments in air quality and comply with instructions and precautionary measures issued by the authorities," it said.
However, parents or guardians who are concerned about their children's health may keep them at home, provided they inform the school accordingly.
The department said any further updates would be communicated through its official channels and those of schools to ensure the public receives accurate and up-to-date information.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran army says any new war with US could be 'longer than previous conflict'
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran warned on Sunday that any new war with the United States could last longer than the previous conflict and that US President Donald Trump would not be the one to determine its duration.
"A potential future war could last longer than previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion," said army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, according to Iranian state television.
He was referring to the most intense phase of the fighting in the war that began on Feb 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, killing the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
Iran responded by launching missiles and drones across the region, while the militant groups it backs also entered the fray in Lebanon and Yemen.
Iran's Defence Minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi on Sunday warned of a "proportionate, decisive, and impactful response" to any attack on the country, according to state TV.
"Those who pose threats will not dictate the scope, timing, or consequences of Iran's defensive response," he added.
Also on Sunday, Hossein Mohebbi, the spokesperson of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran's military, echoed the remarks made by the country's new supreme leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei in a written message the day before.
"In a conflict with America, there are no geographical limitations; a vast theatre has been defined for inflicting damage upon the enemy," Mohebbi said, according to state TV.
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that the United States has knocked out much of Iran's military but still has to "take care of" one or two targets.
"We've knocked out their nuclear. We still have to take care of, I would say one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes," Trump said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: MCMC won't interfere in online campaigns, will act only upon complaints
Article:
MELAKA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will not interfere in social media campaigns by political parties contesting the Melaka election, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
Instead, he said the commission would actively monitor social media platforms and only initiate investigations or take action against posts upon receiving complaints from the public.
"To date, these are the only two mechanisms MCMC will apply to posts related to campaigning by contesting parties on social media platforms," he said when asked about the commission's online monitoring measures during the Melaka election, scheduled for Nov 14.
Fahmi said this at a press conference after attending the Safe Internet Programme at the Multimedia University (MMU) Melaka Campus in Bukit Beruang today.
He said MCMC was also monitoring the misuse of social media accounts to spread false information, the use of deepfakes and the dissemination of extremely offensive content.
"We are also tracking a trend where content is uploaded by fake accounts, which then disappear once the posts are published.
"This happens frequently and is not something we anticipate only during the state election. It is being detected more often and is quite worrying.
"We found that much of the content containing derogatory statements against the King originated from overseas-based accounts. Upon closer examination, we found that most of them, or 98 per cent, were fake accounts, so we take this very seriously," he said.
Asked about Pakatan Harapan's decision to name Parti Amanah Negara vice-president Adly Zahari as its Chief Minister candidate, Fahmi said the decision was based on his experience.
"He is an experienced figure. He has served as a state assemblyman for two terms and was previously Chief Minister," said Fahmi, who is also PH communications director.
PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari was previously reported as saying that Adly, who is the coalition's candidate for the Bukit Katil constituency, had been chosen as its poster boy and candidate for Chief Minister should PH win the Melaka election.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the election, with early voting scheduled for Nov 10.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Portuguese police clash with housing protesters, arrest 13
Article:
LISBON: Riot police with dogs stormed protest camps in Lisbon and Porto early Sunday, charging demonstrators with batons, arresting 13 people and leaving dozens injured in the latest confrontation over Portugal's housing crisis.
Clashes quickly broke out as dozens of officers moved in on an encampment in Lisbon's Rossio Square and a smaller camp in Porto's Dom Joao I Square at around 4.30am.
Protesters shouted "smells like a dictatorship", while police said some hurled bottles and paint at officers as they tried to take down the tents.
Police said in a statement that six people were arrested in Lisbon and seven in Porto for refusing orders to disperse. It said 13 police were injured in the process, with eight taken to hospital.
In Porto, police said three plain-clothes officers monitoring the protesters were assaulted after being spotted by a group.
One of the officers displayed his firearm as a deterrent, police said.
An unspecified number of civilians were also injured during the operation, which was carried out "with rigour, balance and respect for citizens' rights", the statement read.
Activist group Acampada Lisboa said more than 30 protesters were injured, including 10 who required hospital treatment, and called a fresh rally in the capital on Sunday afternoon to protest against the police operation.
"We will not be silenced," it said in a statement posted on social media, alongside photographs of protesters with bruises or bleeding from injuries it blamed on "police violence."
Some protesters carried red carnations, a symbol of Portugal's 1974 revolution, evoking the peaceful military-led uprising that ended nearly five decades of dictatorship.
Police said they seized 69 tents in Lisbon and 30 in Porto.
The camps had been set up late Saturday after peaceful marches through the two cities against soaring housing costs.
Officers have repeatedly dismantled encampments that have sprung up across Lisbon and Porto in recent weeks.
'DARK NIGHT'
After police cleared protest camps in the two cities last weekend, Amnesty International said it was "deeply concerned by the excessive and disproportionate use of force by police."
A lawyer representing protesters at Lisbon's housing camps, Ricardo Sa Fernandes, said Sunday he would file a criminal complaint against the interior minister and the national police chief for abuse of power.
"This is a dark night in the history of Portuguese democracy. This is absolutely intolerable and has crossed all limits," he told reporters outside a police station in Lisbon where some of those detained were taken.
Protesters want the minority centre-right government to abandon plans to ease evictions and remove rent caps on new leases, warning the measures would push up housing costs and leave tenants more vulnerable.
Prime Minister Luis Montenegro has acknowledged that property prices have doubled in a decade, but blames the crisis on previous left-wing governments for failing to build enough homes and pursuing what he calls an overly permissive migration policy.
Portuguese protesters have taken inspiration from a similar movement in neighbouring Spain, where tents have stood in central Madrid and other cities for weeks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Duyong incumbent: 'For five years, we have been on the ground'
Article:
KOTA MELAKA: Duyong incumbent and Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem is banking on his five-year track record as he seeks re-election in Melaka.
He said voters wanted a representative they knew, could approach and rely on to help resolve problems affecting the community.
Mohd Noor Helmy said residents expected their elected representative to be visible and accessible, whether through social media or face-to-face engagement.
He said his experience serving the constituency had given him a better understanding of residents' needs, particularly in household welfare, public safety and basic infrastructure.
He said residents wanted sufficient household income to meet daily expenses, safe and comfortable surroundings, and proper roads and drainage to prevent flooding.
"For five years, we have been on the ground and understand what the people actually need. They are not asking for high-rise buildings or shopping malls. They want their daily needs taken care of," he said.
Mohd Noor Helmy said development proposals should also be assessed against Duyong's needs, with unsuitable projects raised through the appropriate channels.
He said voters should assess incumbents based on their work, results and efforts over the past five years, while considering the promises made by challengers.
Among the initiatives during his tenure was a medical crowdfunding effort through social media, which helped families seek public contributions for expensive treatment, including liver transplants and cancer medication.
He said the initiative, which began about two years ago, had also attracted contributions from outside Duyong, with some cases coming from other parts of Melaka and Negri Sembilan.
He added that the funeral management programme involving four mosques in the constituency provided free funeral arrangements and first-night meals for bereaved Muslim families.
He said it reflected his approach of addressing practical needs at the community level.
Mohd Noor Helmy is facing Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Poo Long Suan, a former Hang Tuah Jaya Municipal Council member.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kelantan Sultan urges graduates to become job creators, not job seekers
Article:
BACHOK: University graduates should shift their focus from seeking employment to creating job opportunities by harnessing artificial intelligence (AI) and the digital economy, which are increasingly transforming the conventional employment landscape.
Sultan of Kelantan Sultan Muhammad V said Universiti Malaysia Kelantan (UMK) graduates, in particular, should view these changes as opportunities to venture into entrepreneurship, develop new business models and create jobs.
His Royal Highness said the entrepreneurial values instilled at UMK should encourage graduates not merely to become job seekers, but also to become architects of opportunities and job creators.
"Master the digital economy and smart technology to develop new business models, pioneer cross-border e-commerce and modernise local market supply chains.
"UMK must be at the forefront of driving artificial intelligence guided by the values of ethics, integrity and trustworthiness," he said.
The royal address was delivered by Tengku Mahkota Kelantan Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra at UMK's 16th Convocation Ceremony at Dewan Tuanku Canselor, UMK Bachok, here today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sell achievements, not slander: Asyraf Wajdi outlines BN's Melaka election strategy
Article:
MASJID TANAH: Barisan Nasional (BN) campaign machinery has been reminded to focus on the coalition's track record and policy offers to the people during the Melaka election campaign, rather than resorting to emotional appeals, slander or personal attacks against political opponents.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said campaigning should centre on explaining the agenda for the people and the state government's achievements over the past four years.
"We are accountable for our performance, not for playing on emotions. We do not need to hurl insults at others or spread slander.
"We should focus on explaining the agenda we want to implement for the people and what we have achieved over the past four years," he said at a meet-and-greet programme with the Taboh Naning state constituency community at the Cherana Puteh polling district centre here today.
Also present was incumbent Taboh Naning assemblyman Datuk Zulkiflee Mohd Zin.
On another matter, Asyraf said cooperation between BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the Melaka election had shown positive progress, with both coalitions' campaign machinery working together at the grassroots level.
"This cooperation is not only at the top leadership level, but also at the division, constituency and supporters' levels. I believe this shows that the grassroots genuinely want this cooperation," he said.
He said the joint BN-PN manifesto, which was initially expected to be launched earlier, had been postponed to Tuesday to allow both coalitions to align their respective offers and agendas.
Asyraf also reminded campaign machinery not to underestimate the competition, urging them to continue engaging with all voter groups regardless of race, age or political leanings ahead of polling on Nov 14.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ab Rauf: Melaka voters, not political rivals, will judge state govt's performance
Article:
MELAKA: Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh maintains that the state government's performance should be measured and judged by the people, not its political rivals.
"I don't know where he (Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Adly Zahari) obtained those findings, but I don't want to comment because he was also once the Chief Minister, and I don't want to comment on what he did during his tenure either.
"So, it is better for us to reflect on ourselves and what we have done for the people. I believe the people of Melaka know what we have done. The only person who doesn't know is him," he said during a visit to the BN operations room for the Telok Mas state constituency here today.
Earlier, Adly had questioned the performance of the BN-led Melaka government despite securing a strong mandate by winning 21 of the 28 seats in the previous state election.
Adly said BN should explain its achievements during its term in office instead of merely asking voters to continue placing their trust in the administration without addressing their grievances.
He said the mandate, which gave BN nearly 75 per cent of the state seats, should have translated into solutions to the people's problems, particularly those involving housing, welfare and employment opportunities.
He also claimed that recurring floods, drainage systems, street lighting and maintenance of public facilities, particularly Melaka Sentral, remained unresolved issues affecting the people.
Ab Rauf, who is the incumbent Bukit Katil assemblyman, said Adly should reflect on his own record.
"Let others engage in (dirty politics). We will focus on talking about what we have done for the people and what they have gained from our administration of the state over the past five years.
"I noticed that the overwhelming support shown by the people yesterday during nomination day, with thousands turning up, reflected strong enthusiasm for us to return to power," he said.
Ab Rauf stressed that BN had started engaging with the people well before the election campaign and did not wait until the 14-day campaigning period to reach out to voters or make promises.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shahrizat says BN reps must serve beyond election periods
Article:
KOTA MELAKA: Veteran Umno leader Tan Sri Shahrizat Abdul Jalil has called on Barisan Nasional (BN) representatives to continue serving their constituents between elections, citing Duyong incumbent Mohd Noor Helmy as an example.
Shahrizat, an Umno Supreme Council member, said Mohd Noor Helmy remained accessible to residents and continued addressing their concerns throughout his term.
She said residents she met during a visit to Duyong had spontaneously expressed support for the incumbent, whom she described as hardworking and consistently present on the ground.
"It is not because he is an influencer. There are many influencers, but what makes him stand out is that he works hard, goes to the ground and engages with the people, not just during elections," she said.
"From what we have seen, whenever he hears about a case, he immediately goes there. He does not know the meaning of being tired," she added after visiting Duyong for the 'Ziarah HAWAcare' programme.
The visit included engagements with three residents and their families facing various difficulties, including loss of household income and serious health issues.
Also present were Wanita Umno chief Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's wife, Datin Seri Hamidah Khamis, and BN candidate Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem.
Shahrizat, who had served several terms as a member of parliament, said BN's political culture had always been to serve the people immediately after receiving their mandate.
She said this applied to both state and parliamentary elections, as public support depended on voters' views of a party's manifesto, services, policies and leadership.
"We cannot become representatives who only appear during election season. That is not our culture. You have to sacrifice your time, energy and other commitments for them," she said.
Asked whether Mohd Noor Helmy's approach could serve as an example for other BN representatives, Shahrizat said his standard of service could be emulated beyond Melaka.
"His legacy and standard of service can be an example not just for Melaka, but for the whole country," she said.
Mohd Noor Helmy said his priorities for Duyong would remain focused on residents' immediate needs, including household welfare, safety and basic infrastructure.
He said the rising cost of daily necessities, road conditions, drainage and flood prevention were more pressing concerns for residents than large-scale development projects that might not necessarily benefit the constituency.
Any development plans, he added, must take Duyong's needs into account. He would speak up against projects that were unsuitable for the area.
Of the 28 seats, 11 will see straight fights, with nine featuring contests between BN and Pakatan Harapan and the remaining two between BN and Bersatu. All 11 were won by BN in 2021.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Klang's Little India bustling despite rain ahead of Deepavali
Article:
KLANG: Hindu shoppers are braving the rain to finish their Deepavali shopping at Klang's Little India ahead of the celebrations on Nov 8.
A Bernama survey today found the enclave, which is home to more than 100 shops, crowded with shoppers buying clothes, jewellery, food and prayer items for the Festival of Lights.
Many visitors also spent the weekend exploring the commercial district with their families, while traders offered discounts.
Engineer S. Meiyarasan, 28, said his family had opted for last-minute shopping while keeping an eye on Klang's weather, which usually brings afternoon downpours.
"Living in Puchong, I check weather updates before travelling anywhere because of the ongoing northeast monsoon season.
"This helps ensure our shopping trip for festive essentials, especially clothes and food, goes smoothly. There is also a wide variety of items at reasonable prices here," he said.
S. Kalaiselvi, 55, described the area as a one-stop destination for Deepavali preparations, saying shopping there had been a family tradition for 20 years. She preferred shopping in person to buying online.
"I prefer shopping in person so I can check the quality and material, especially for festive attire such as sarees and dhotis for the family.
"Rain may cause some inconvenience, but completing our preparations is important for a festival celebrated only once a year," said the mother of two.
Sri Kumaran Textile owner N. Ravi Chandran, 62, said his store had extended its opening hours until midnight to cater to high customer demand, despite afternoon rain.
"Mornings are usually clear or hot, but afternoon rain means we have to keep the shop open until midnight. Nearly 2,000 customers visit, particularly at weekends.
"The festive atmosphere in the final week before Deepavali has become lively, with discounts ranging from 30 to 50 per cent. We have 35 staff members to manage the demand," he said.
Former factory worker M. Sarkunan, 66, said Klang's Little India had long been his preferred shopping destination because of its affordable prices, particularly for B40 households buying clothes and festive treats such as murukku and suji biscuits.
"Prices here are more than 10 per cent cheaper, which helps me save before I return to celebrate at my child's house in Kulim, Kedah," said the grandfather of two from Kapar.— BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN began engaging voters long before Melaka polls, says Ab Rauf
Article:
MELAKA: The first day of campaigning for the 16th Melaka election was relatively calmer than previous elections, says Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
He attributed this to BN's early efforts to engage with the people, rather than limiting its outreach to the 14-day campaign period.
"We have started our work earlier so that the people are not only given attention during elections, particularly throughout the 14-day campaign period.
"Therefore, we must regard the position of an elected representative as a trust to serve the people, not for the people to serve us," he said.
He was speaking during a visit to the BN operations room for the Telok Mas state constituency here today.
Ab Rauf said the Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat (WRUR) programme had resolved about 75 per cent of the 4,800 complaints received.
He said he had also stressed the importance of BN candidates understanding the people's needs before being elected as their representatives.
"Among the things I emphasised in my vision for selecting candidates to become elected representatives is that they must first be part of the people.
"They need to understand the people's problems and needs, listen to their views and convey them to me so that the government can formulate appropriate policies in the future.
"Through the WRUR programme, we successfully identified 1,001 problems and resolved about 75 per cent of the 4,800 complaints received, based on the people's needs," he said.
Commenting further, Ab Rauf said the calm campaign atmosphere should not be marred by what he described as the politics of hatred played by his opponents.
Instead, Melaka BN would continue using the campaign period to engage with voters and explain the state government's achievements.
"Let others do that. We will focus on talking about what we have implemented for the people and the benefits they have received throughout our five years administering the state," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nga: Housing must put people and communities first
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Housing development must prioritise affordability, liveability and community well-being rather than treating homes as commercial commodities, Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said.
Nga, who is also president of the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) Assembly, said urban progress should not be measured solely by the number of skyscrapers, but by improvements in community well-being.
He said this required a focus on four key pillars: affordability, liveability, connectivity and access to essential amenities.
"Housing should not merely be treated as a commodity for buying and selling but as a place where every family can build a secure and stable life. We must not only ensure that people can afford to buy a home, but also that they can live with peace of mind, comfort and dignity," he said.
He was speaking at the World Cities Day 2026 Forum on "Building High Quality Housing for the People" in Fuzhou, China.
Nga said meeting these benchmarks required coordinated action by governments, builders, developers and the wider community.
He said people-centred urban planning should combine housing with public transport, schools, medical centres and recreational spaces to build connected communities.
"Good housing must be supported by the facilities and services people need. High-rise buildings alone cannot create a community without human connection," he said.
Nga urged municipal authorities and builders to adopt artificial intelligence, green building frameworks and smart construction technologies to improve building quality, energy efficiency and resilience to climate disruptions and natural hazards.
He said urban development should be judged by improvements in people's quality of life, rather than the number of skyscrapers built.
On regional cooperation, he said the Ipoh Accord, established at the Fourth Asean-China Ministerial Roundtable on Construction and Housing in Perak on Aug 1, underpinned cross-border initiatives in low-carbon design, urban renewal and community environment upgrading.
Nga said he was confident that Malaysia-China and Asean-China partnerships would drive sustainable development for future generations.
"We do not inherit the Earth from our ancestors; we borrow it from our children. The homes and communities we build today must serve not only the present generation but also those to come," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thousands protest in India's capital against voter roll revision
Article:
NEW DELHI: Thousands joined a protest led by opposition politicians in India's capital on Sunday, renewing demands for the country's election chief to resign over an overhaul of voter lists they say unfairly benefits the ruling party.
The nationwide revision of electoral rolls has sparked political disputes and street protests in the world's largest democracy over the last month.
The Election Commission says the initiative is necessary to ensure accurate voter lists, but the opposition claims it is being manipulated to favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Both the Election Commission and the BJP deny the accusations.
On Sunday, protesters led by opposition Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi chanted "vote thief, leave your seat" and beat drums while marching from central parts of New Delhi to Ramlila Maidan, a large outdoor venue.
"I have been a voter since I was 18 and now I find myself struck off the list," protester Nandita, 46, told AFP, giving only one name.
"It's important to be here because of the way things are going. The cost of living is going up... The only option is to take to the streets peacefully."
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online youth-led protest movement, has also thrown its weight behind the campaign against the voter-roll revision.
The overhaul of India's voter rolls has resulted in more than 133 million names being removed from electoral lists, according to figures reported by Indian media and cited by opposition parties in court filings.
Critics say the removals have disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims.
[[nid:1568447]]
Members of Hindu-nationalist BJP have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India's electoral rolls.
Election authorities say the revision was intended to eliminate duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries, and that eligible voters remain entitled to apply for inclusion on the roll.
Human Rights Watch has said the removal of voters was "arbitrary and deeply flawed."
"The authorities should immediately scrap the voter roll revision process that has denied India's most marginalised people their right to vote and other government services," it said in a statement this week.
The Cockroach movement has been heavily involved in the pushback to the voter-roll revision and several of its leaders were temporarily detained by police during protests last month.
The CJP has gained millions of followers on social media since it was launched in May.
Earlier protests organised by the CJP in July over exam irregularities forced the resignation of the education minister, marking a rare climbdown by Modi's administration.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: With no majority, what options remain for Israel's Netanyahu, Eisenkot?
Article:
FOLLOWING elections in which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his main rival Gadi Eisenkot both fell short of a majority, each is claiming a mandate to govern – though neither has explained how.
Given the indecisive result, the two leaders would need to find a way to broaden their blocs if they hope to secure a governing coalition, but so far very little information has leaked about potential behind-the-scenes negotiations.
If neither succeeds in securing a coalition, the country will have to head back to the polls.
AFP looks at the most plausible scenarios for each side forming a government.
A Netanyahu-led government
The prime minister and his far-right and ultra-Orthodox allies came out ahead in the final vote count, with 53 seats in parliament, including 27 for the premier's party, Likud.
But that is still short of the 61 needed for a majority.
If he hopes to stay in power, Netanyahu will have to reach out to opposition parties with a pitch to join his government – a major about-face after a campaign run on vows to unseat him.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog, who is tasked with tapping the candidate best positioned to form a coalition, has said a new vote must be avoided at all costs.
Of the four parties in Eisenkot's camp, the least receptive to an overture from Netanyahu would be the left-wing Democrats, led by Yair Golan, which won eight seats.
Netanyahu's former ally turned fierce critic Avigdor Lieberman, whose right-wing Yisrael Beiteinu party won seven seats, would also likely dismiss the prospect out of hand.
Lieberman said on Thursday that "the only conceivable coalition" was one without Netanyahu, though he suggested the rest of the premier's party would be tolerated.
The stance of Naftali Bennett's centre-right Together party, which won 12 seats, is less clear.
Bennett had initially suggested he would not oppose an alliance with Netanyahu's camp under certain conditions, notably the immediate creation of a commission of inquiry into the Oct 7, 2023 attacks.
But he later backtracked and insisted his remarks had been misconstrued.
Finally, the possibility of an alliance with Eisenkot's Yashar party, which nabbed 21 seats, seems remote given the ex-general built his campaign around promises to remove Netanyahu, who he said was unfit to lead.
There is a recent precedent for unlikely power-sharing scenarios. In 2020, Netanyahu and centrist Benny Gantz overcame their deep antipathy to strike a deal to rotate the prime ministership, but the partnership collapsed after a year.
Eisenkot has repeatedly ruled out such an arrangement, saying before the vote: "There will be no form of rotation in the post of prime minister. There will be only one prime minister, and it will be me."
[[nid:1568434]]
Outside the opposition camp, there remains the highly improbable option of Netanyahu turning to Arab-majority lists, with their 19 seats.
The prime minister spent the campaign casting them as bogeymen, and in the days since the vote has accused them of electoral fraud.
But nothing is out of the question when it comes to Netanyahu, a canny political operator who reached out to Arab parties in 2015 and 2021.
An Eisenkot-led government
By refusing to deliver a majority to Netanyahu's camp, the Israeli people "have chosen change", Eisenkot proclaimed on election night.
With his camp holding 48 seats, and having ruled out a power-sharing deal with Netanyahu, Eisenkot has two options going forward: establishing a minority government supported from the outside by other parties, or attempting to broaden his coalition by bringing in Arab lawmakers or defectors from the other camp.
The two Arab-majority groupings, Raam and the Joint List, emerged with eight and 11 seats, respectively.
Raam leader Mansour Abbas joined a short-lived coalition once before, and has voiced willingness to do so again, but that option is opposed by some parties in the opposition bloc.
The Joint List's Yousef Jabareen, meanwhile, has said he is willing to support Eisenkot in parliament but without joining his government, expressing discomfort with, among other things, the war in Gaza.
Taken together, the Arab lists would give Eisenkot the seats he needs to move forward, but relying on them would mean going back on a campaign promise and gambling on a fragile minority government that observers say would be unlikely to last long.
A former army chief, Eisenkot is not a pacifist, and the possibility of future military operations – including in Gaza, where he has pledged to end Hamas rule in 18 months – could prompt his new allies to pull their support.
Eisenkot could also try to woo away defectors from Netanyahu's camp.
Defections from the Likud are improbable given how firmly the party is aligned behind the premier, and its far-right allies are considered politically unpalatable to the change bloc.
But the remaining ultra-Orthodox parties currently aligned with Netanyahu, who hold 13 seats, could prove more amenable.
Eisenkot – who lost a son in the Gaza war – has argued forcefully for ending military service exemptions for the ultra-Orthodox community, which those parties oppose, though they could be willing to jump ship in the event of concessions from one side or the other.
* The article is from AFP
